subject: general
question: The 'right to property' is a:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Legal right**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 'right to property' was originally a Fundamental Right under Article 31 of the Constitution of India.
 
• However, it was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.
 
• Currently, the 'right to property' is a **Legal right** under Article 300A.
 
• As a Legal right, it ensures that no person shall be deprived of his property except by authority of law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 44th Amendment Act was passed in 1978 during the tenure of the Janata Party government.
 
• The amendment removed the 'right to property' from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a constitutional legal right.
 
• The purpose of this amendment was to facilitate land reforms and prevent the concentration of land in the hands of a few.
 
• As a Legal right, any deprivation of property must be in accordance with the procedure established by law, ensuring protection against arbitrary action by the state.
